title: Perfect squares and difference of squares
keyIdea: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b². A square of side a + b holds a², two ab strips and a b² corner, so the middle term is doubled. a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b). Cut a b by b corner from a², and the L that is left rearranges into an (a + b) by (a − b) rectangle. Root both parts first: 4x² − 25 = (2x + 5)(2x − 5).

kid: Take a square that is x long on each side. Make each side 3 longer. The new square is (x + 3) by (x + 3).
Look at the pieces. There is the old x by x square. There are two thin strips, each x by 3. And there is a small 3 by 3 square in the corner. So (x + 3)² = x² + 3x + 3x + 9, which is x² + 6x + 9.
Now go the other way. Start with x² and cut a 3 by 3 square off one corner. What is left is x² − 9. It looks like an L.
Cut the thin part off the L and turn it. It fits on the end. Now you have a box shape that is x + 3 long and x − 3 wide. So x² − 9 = (x + 3)(x − 3).
adult: Squaring a bracket gives a perfect square: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b². The picture shows why the middle term is doubled. A square of side a + b holds one a by a square, two a by b strips and one b by b corner.

To spot one, check that the first and last terms are squares. Then check that the middle term is twice the product of their roots. x² + 10x + 25 = (x + 5)², since 25 = 5² and 10 = 2 × 5. x² + 10x + 20 is not one, because 20 is not a square.

The difference of two squares is a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b). Cut a b by b corner from an a by a square. The L that is left turns into an (a + b) by (a − b) rectangle. Expanding gives a² − ab + ab − b², and the middle terms cancel. It speeds up sums too: 23 × 17 = 20² − 3² = 391, and 21² = 400 + 40 + 1 = 441.

Common mistakes: writing (x + 3)² as x² + 9; keeping only one strip, so x² + 3x + 9; writing (x − 3)² for x² − 9; leaving the number unrooted, as in (x + 9)(x − 9); not rooting the 4 in 4x² − 25, which gives (4x + 5)(4x − 5) instead of (2x + 5)(2x − 5); and trying to factorise a sum such as x² + 9, which has no real factors.

familyTip: Cut a 10 by 10 square from squared paper. Cut a 3 by 3 square from one corner, then snip off the thin strip and move it to the end. Count the new rectangle: 13 by 7 = 91, which is 100 − 9.

worked.title: Factorise 25x² − 36, then check by expanding.
steps: Both terms are squares: 25x² = (5x)² and 36 = 6². They are subtracted, so this is a difference of two squares.
Use a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b) with a = 5x and b = 6: 25x² − 36 = (5x + 6)(5x − 6).
Careful: (25x + 36)(25x − 36) forgets the roots, and (5x − 6)² would expand to 25x² − 60x + 36.

practice.prompt: Expand (x + {n})². What is the coefficient of x?
practice.hint: There are two strips, each {n} by x. Add them.
practice.explain: (x + {n})² = x² + {n}x + {n}x + {=n*n} = x² + {=2*n}x + {=n*n}, so the coefficient is {=2*n}.

practice.hint: This is a difference of two squares: ({a} + 3)({a} − 3) = {a}² − 3².
practice.explain: {a}² − 3² = {=a*a} − 9 = {=a*a-9}. The 3 by 3 corner is taken away.
x² − 49 = (x + 7)(x − 7). (x − 7)² gives x² − 14x + 49, and 49 must be rooted to 7.

practice.prompt: Which of these is a perfect square?
practice.hint: The last term must be a square, and the middle term must be twice its root times x.
practice.explain: x² + 8x + 16 = (x + 4)²: 16 = 4² and 8 = 2 × 4. x² + 16 has no middle term, and 8 is not a square.

practice.hint: 9x² is the square of 3x, and 4 is the square of 2.

pool.hint: Write it as (x − 5)(x − 5) and multiply every part.
pool.explain: x² − 5x − 5x + 25 = x² − 10x + 25. The corner is (−5) × (−5) = +25, and x² − 25 drops the middle term.

pool.prompt: (x + {n})² = x² + bx + c. What is c?
pool.hint: c is the corner square, {n} by {n}.
pool.explain: c = {n} × {n} = {=n*n}. Not {=2*n}: that is the middle coefficient b.

choices: It cannot be factorised with real numbers
pool.hint: Expand each option and compare with x² + 25.
pool.explain: (x + 5)(x − 5) = x² − 25 and (x + 5)² = x² + 10x + 25. A sum of two squares has no real factors.

pool.prompt: Sam writes (x + 4)² = x² + 16. What went wrong?
choices: He dropped the two strips: the middle term 8x is missing
pool.hint: Draw the square of side x + 4. How many pieces does it have?
pool.explain: (x + 4)² = x² + 4x + 4x + 16 = x² + 8x + 16. Squaring each part alone leaves out the two x by 4 strips.

pool.hint: Expand the brackets. The x terms cancel.
Multiply out. What happens to +6x and −6x?
pool.explain: x² − 6x + 6x − 36 = x² − 36. The middle terms cancel, and +6 × −6 is −36.

pool.hint: 49 = 7², and the middle term is negative.
pool.explain: x² − 14x + 49 = (x − 7)², since (−7)² = 49 and 2 × (−7) = −14. (x + 7)(x − 7) has no middle term.
